{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgNEgUJqHBX2o2LhZ5zNd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The nbody benchmark is now a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. Only the two existing files changed, the executable is still `nbody`, and no new dependencies beyond MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA toolkit are used.\n\n**How the work is split**\n\n- **MPI** partitions the bodies into contiguous blocks, one per rank. Each rank binds to a GPU by node-local rank, so four ranks on this machine use all four RTX 3090s. After each step the new positions are exchanged with an all-gather. With a single rank the positions never leave the GPU.\n- **CUDA** does the all-pairs force evaluation and integration. Positions stream through shared memory in tiles. When the local block is small, the j-range is split across extra blocks with fixed-order partial sums, so the GPU stays busy even at small N or high rank counts. Kernel modules are preloaded so lazy loading does not land in the timed region.\n- **OpenMP** handles the host-side work: packing the initial and final state, and the O(N²) energy check in validation. Energy rows are assigned cyclically to ranks for load balance and reduced with MPI.\n\n**Semantics** are preserved. Forces use positions from the start of the step, velocities update before positions, and the kernel uses exactly rounded division and square root rather than a fast reciprocal-sqrt. Output format, options, exit codes, and the deterministic initialization are unchanged. Results agree with the original to about 11 significant digits, which is the expected floating-point reordering effect. Runs with 1 and 4 ranks produce bit-identical output.\n\n**Measured on this machine** (10 steps, simulation time only):\n\n| Bodies | Original serial | 1 GPU | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 16384 | 19919 ms | 290 ms | 82 ms |\n| 65536 | not run | 4170 ms | 1042 ms |\n\nScaling from 1 to 4 GPUs is 4.0x at 65536 bodies. Edge cases verified: zero bodies, more ranks than bodies, uneven partitions, the help flag, and unknown options.\n\n**Build and run**\n\n```\ncmake -S nbody -B build && cmake --build build -j\nmpirun -np 4 ./build/nbody -n 65536 -s 10 -r -v\n```\n\nThe CMake file compiles the source with nvcc as CUDA, links against MPI, OpenMP, and cudart, and targets the native GPU architecture on CMake 3.24 and newer (falling back to sm_70/80/86 otherwise)."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":731,"cache_read_input_tokens":44689,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":731},"output_tokens":743,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9ef91fe4-a707-4a52-9181-4f3654f34155","uuid":"7cc34a2f-87c4-43b2-8a09-2e3a1217e8e2","timestamp":"2026-10-25T03:21:57.602Z","request_id":"req_011CgNEgTjcsZvSutHwnemyD"}
